name: MCP Client
description: Connect to Model Context Protocol servers, expose their tools to the Finch, and provide an mcp.client capability for other extensions.
systemPrompt: Use MCP with action=list/add/edit/remove to manage configured MCP services; never ask users to paste secrets in chat, because add/edit opens a secure form for secret values. For HTTP add/edit, set authMethod to none, oauth, bearer, basic, or apiKey; for API keys also pass apiKeyPlacement and apiKeyName, and use headerNames for extra business headers. Pass only non-secret metadata — the secure form collects passwords, tokens, API keys, and header values, then add/edit waits for a successful connection. Protocol headers (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param-*) are generated automatically by the client per request — never configure them as fixed custom headers, because Mcp-Name must match the request body's params.name/params.uri; a HeaderMismatch/-32020 or missing-Mcp-Name error points to client/transport protocol issues (negotiated version, SDK version, transport wrapper), not a missing custom header. To use MCP server tools, first call Finch's standard ToolSearch with source:'mcp:<server>' when the target server is known; use source:'mcp' only if that precise search finds no usable tool. ToolSearch connects the selected servers, discovers tools, and injects matching mcp__<server>__<tool> functions into the current run. Authorization can be granted per-tool (mcp__filesystem__read_file) or with a wildcard (mcp__filesystem__*).

form.add.title: Add MCP server
form.add.description: Review and complete the configuration for "{name}". Secret values stay on your machine.
form.edit.title: Edit MCP server "{name}"
form.edit.description: Review and update the configuration. Leave secret fields blank to keep them unchanged.
confirm.remove.title: Remove MCP server "{name}"?
confirm.remove.message:
! The configuration and any saved credentials are deleted. This cannot be undone.

The server disconnects immediately; using it again means going through setup from scratch.
confirm.remove.cancelled: User cancelled the removal. MCP server "{name}" is unchanged.
field.name: Server name
field.header.description: Sent with every HTTP request. The value is stored securely on this device.
field.token.desc.bearerAdd: Paste the raw token only (no "Bearer" prefix). Sent as "Authorization: Bearer <token>". Leave blank if the server needs no auth.
field.token.desc.customAdd: Sent as the "{header}" header. Leave blank if the server needs no auth.
field.token.desc.keep: Leave blank to keep the existing token.
field.token.desc.bearerEdit: Paste the raw token only (no "Bearer" prefix). Sent as "Authorization: Bearer <token>". Leave blank for no auth.
field.token.desc.customEdit: Sent as the "{header}" header. Leave blank for no auth.
error.invalidUrl: The endpoint is invalid. Enter a complete URL beginning with http:// or https://.
error.inlineCredential: The URL appears to contain a credential. Use API key with URL query placement so the secure form can store it safely.
error.nameConflict.user: A custom MCP server named “{name}” already exists. Use a different name.
error.nameConflict.extension: The “{owner}” Mini Tool already provides an MCP server named “{name}”. Use a different name.
